A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ChartAgent paper, including all 69 pages and Appendices A–N. Text, embedded-content, and rendered-page comparisons establish matching substantive material; differences are confined to the arXiv version/date stamp and associated metadata.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original ChartAgent evaluations on ChartBench and ChartX (Table 1), an internal dataset (Table 15), and ablation, recovery, and failure analyses.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the original benchmark evaluations, internal-dataset results, ablations, and analyses reported in v2.pdf.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical routing, ReAct reasoning, chart-specific tools, visual self-verification, in-context examples, and fallback procedures. The tool specifications and prompts in the appendices also match.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ChartBench and ChartX coverage and the same 125-pair internal dataset in Appendix L.6.2. Chart types, annotation conditions, and question-answering tasks are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the main benchmark tables, ablation comparison, and concurrent-model evaluations. Tables 1, 10, 14, and 15 retain the same methods in their respective experiments.

E3.justification: Dataset filtering and sample counts, model configurations, prompting protocols, the 15-iteration limit, response standardization, and 5% numerical tolerance are unchanged. Appendix evaluation and analysis procedures also match.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical tool ablations, numerical-tolerance sensitivity, complexity analyses, recovery and fallback studies, qualitative trajectories, and failure analyses in Sections 5.2–5.4 and the appendices.

E5.justification: Appendix G retains the same fixed random seed of 42. Sampling descriptions and statistical reporting are identical, with no added or removed repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, ChartAgent retains 71.39% ChartBench and 59.69% ChartX overall accuracy in Table 1, and 85.19% accuracy with 3.42% average error in Table 15.

T1.justification: The state-update formulation in Section 3.1 and mathematical content in the tool specifications are identical. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about visually grounded chart reasoning, the tool library, benchmark performance, and generalization across underlying models.

C2.justification: Interpretations of tool effectiveness, possible benchmark leakage, recovery behavior, and computational tradeoffs are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning task coverage, latency, tool evaluation, and difficult chart formats.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures match, including AutoGen and Python versions, model identifiers, hardware, tool specifications, prompts, runtime, and cost information. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B, and the reference list are identical. Neither cited works nor positioning relative to chart-VQA methods, visual grounding, and agentic frameworks changes.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 7 Jan 2026 to v3 dated 8 Jun 2026. The title, authors, prose, headings, and appendix organization are identical.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, and their placement are identical throughout the main text and appendices. Rendered differences are confined to the updated first-page version/date margin stamp.

improvement.justification: The later PDF preserves the same methods, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information, including all appendices. Updating the arXiv stamp and metadata produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
